title: Weighted conformal prediction under covariate shift: process limits, estimated weights and efficiency
abstract: arXiv:2611.20052v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Weighted split conformal prediction handles covariate shift by reweighting calibration scores with the likelihood ratio $v=dQ_X/dP_X$; its training-conditional coverage is a functional of the self-normalized weighted empirical distribution function $\hat F_m$, and we study the process $\sqrt m(\hat F_m-F_Q)$. It converges in $\ell^\infty$ to the Gaussian process $W(G(t))-F_Q(t)W(K^2)$, with $G(t)=\mathbb{E}_Q[v\mathbf{1}\{S\le t\}]$ and $K^2=1+\chi^2(Q\|P)$, if and only if $\chi^2(Q\|P)<\infty$ (for non-degenerate scores); $\sup v$ plays no role. The limit gives the joint law of the coverage across levels, consistent bootstraps, inflations asymptotically exact uniformly in the level, and Berry-Esseen-type rates. With estimated ratios, a uniform expansion remains valid when the estimate uses the calibration covariates; the estimation error enters through a covariance term that can reduce the variance below the oracle's, and a pairs boot

translated_title: 协变量偏移下的加权保形预测：过程极限、估计权重与效率
translated_abstract: 加权分裂保形预测通过用似然比 $v=dQ_X/dP_X$ 对校准分数重新加权来处理协变量偏移；其训练条件覆盖率是自归一化加权经验分布函数 $\hat F_m$ 的泛函，本文研究了过程 $\sqrt m(\hat F_m-F_Q)$。当且仅当 $\chi^2(Q\|P)<\infty$ 时（对非退化分数而言），该过程在 $\ell^\infty$ 中收敛到高斯过程 $W(G(t))-F_Q(t)W(K^2)$，其中 $G(t)=\mathbb{E}_Q[v\mathbf{1}\{S\le t\}]$ 且 $K^2=1+\chi^2(Q\|P)$；而 $\sup v$ 不起任何作用。该极限给出了跨置信水平的覆盖率的联合分布、一致的 bootstrap 方法、在水平上一致渐近精确的膨胀系数，以及 Berry-Esseen 型收敛速率。在使用估计比率的情况下，只要估计使用了校准协变量，一致展开仍然有效；估计误差通过一个协方差项进入，该协方差项可使方差降低到低于 oracle 权重的方差水平，此外还有成对的 boot……（摘要截断）
tldr: 本文建立了协变量偏移下加权保形预测中自归一化加权经验过程的核心极限定理，证明收敛当且仅当 $\chi^2$ 散度有限（而非 $\sup v$），由此导出跨水平覆盖率的联合分布、一致性 bootstrap、渐近精确的膨胀系数与 Berry-Esseen 速率，并揭示用校准协变量估计的权重可能比 oracle 权重更高效。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes the central process limit theorem for weighted conformal prediction under covariate shift—showing convergence holds if and only if the χ²-divergence is finite—and derives joint coverage laws, consistent bootstraps, asymptotically exact inflation factors, and Berry-Esseen rates, while revealing that estimated weights using calibration covariates can be more efficient than oracle weights.
